title: PowerShell compatibility profile
description: Declares which PowerShell version's OBSERVABLE SEMANTICS a BrowserShell session emulates. A profile is data, never code: the engine reads it at boot and the same command implementation behaves differently under different profiles. Adding a version must never mean forking a command.

displayVersion.description: What the session banner and $PSVersionTable report. Must equal source.releaseTag minus its leading v, or be explicitly justified in notes.

inherits.description: Profile id this one is a delta against. Resolution is deep-merge: behaviors and command patches from the parent apply first, then this profile's. Cycles are a hard error.

source.description: Provenance. Every field here is copied from the release-truth lockfile, never typed by hand.

derivedFrom.description: Which lockfile generation produced this profile.

bundledModules.description: Modules shipped in the box at this version, as stated by the release notes.

behaviors.description: The semantic switchboard. Every entry is a behavior a command implementation may branch on. Keys are dotted, stable, and documented; a key is added here BEFORE any command reads it.

behaviorDocs.description: Human explanation plus upstream citation for each behavior key. A behavior without a doc entry fails validation in CI: an undocumented flag is a guess.

emulated.description: Whether anything under src/ names this behavior key. Computed at generation time by searching the source, never hand-written. False means the difference is DOCUMENTED, not modelled -- the explorer must say so, because presenting the two identically is the claim of fidelity this project exists to avoid making.

commands.description: Per-command availability and metadata patches, applied over the base command manifest. Absent command means inherit from parent profile.

engineLimits.description: Where BrowserShell knowingly diverges from upstream. Stating a limit is mandatory; silently behaving differently is not allowed.
